evidence.excerpt: LoRa devices operating in the 868 MHz European sub-GHz band are subject to harmonised standard EN 301 489-1 under the Radio Equipment Directive. This paper documents a structured compliance assessment of fifteen commercial and prototype LoRa end-node designs tested for radiated emissions, radiated immunity, and conducted disturbances. Testing was conducted in a semi-anechoic chamber accredited to EN ISO/IEC 17025. Nine of fifteen devices exhibited radiated emissions exceeding the limit in the range 500–1000 MHz under worst-case payload and spreading factor combinations. A correlation between PCB layout quality metrics—specifically, return current path continuity and decoupling capacitor placement—and margin to the emission limit was observed. Immunity tests at 3 V/m field strength revealed functional degradation in four devices manifested as packet loss rates exceeding 10 %. The paper discusses how LoRa duty cycle restrictions interact with the quasi-peak detector integration time specified in the standard, a point of ambiguity that affects reproducibility across laboratories.
